facts.state_of_play: Nearly a week after the Nov. 3 midterms, in which Democrats won both houses of Congress, Trump questioned the results without evidence on Truth Social Monday, reviving voting-machine claims after saying he accepted the outcome and might deal with Democrats. The administration asked the Supreme Court to make California set aside about 20,000 mail-in ballots, and DOJ is appealing dismissal of an Alaska Senate election suit. Officials are also leaving: Civil Division head Brett Shumate resigned Monday, and WH deputy chief of staff Richard Walters resigned Friday, amid a wave of post-midterm departures as Stephen Miller becomes chief of staff. Trump also ordered DOJ on Saturday to investigate members of Congress who proposed impeaching AG Blanche. Blanche signaled on CNN Sunday that Democrats could be investigated, and Sen. Elissa Slotkin's lawyer warned him not to obey Trump's demand to investigate her. Congressional Republicans are in turmoil after losing at least 30 House seats: House and Senate GOP leadership elections are set for Tuesday. Ron Johnson and four allies want the Senate vote delayed, targeting John Thune, while John Barrasso is seeking another term as whip.
